claims.text: Machine-learning-guided severe plastic deformation with programmed strain gradients creates a heterostructured microstructure in conventional alloys.
The resulting heterostructured microstructure overcomes the traditional strength-ductility trade-off.
The proposed starting materials are conventional structural metals or alloys with homogeneous, uniform-grain-size microstructures.
The intervention uses high-pressure torsion at approximately 6 GPa for 10 torsion cycles.
Localized strain gradients are imposed during high-pressure torsion.
Machine learning is used to optimize deformation parameters, including strain rate.
Distinct regions of the material experience different strain rates during deformation.
The intervention produces a gradient microstructure containing juxtaposed ultrafine-grained and coarse-grained zones.
The ultrafine-grained zones provide strength.
The coarser-grained zones provide ductility.
Juxtaposition of ultrafine and coarse grain zones enhances strain partitioning.
Enhanced strain partitioning delays strain localization.
The heterogeneous microstructure enables multiple deformation mechanisms to operate concurrently.
Concurrent deformation mechanisms reduce early strain localization.
The proposed mechanism delays yielding while maintaining high strength.
The proposed processing method increases yield strength relative to conventionally processed counterparts.
The proposed processing method increases ultimate tensile strength relative to conventionally processed counterparts.
The proposed processing method maintains improved ductility relative to conventionally processed counterparts.
The method is expected to be effective for ductile metals capable of undergoing severe plastic deformation.
The method may require modification or have limited applicability for brittle materials or materials with substantially different compositions.
